BURT JONES.name: Burt Jones
BURT JONES.background: Lieutenant governor since 2023 and a business owner from Jackson, Georgia, who served in the legislature from 2012. He won the 2022 Republican primary for lieutenant governor with 50.06%, avoiding a runoff by 813 votes, and the general election with 51.4%. He lost the June 16, 2026 Republican runoff for governor to Rick Jackson, 47.36% to 52.64%.
endorsements: Donald Trump endorsed him in the 2022 primary for lieutenant governor and was described as backing him in the 2026 runoff for governor

sources.t: Yahoo News: Winning by the slimmest of margins, Trump-backed Burt Jones avoids runoff (May 2022)
Washington Post: Georgia primary runoff elections live results, June 16, 2026

ANDRE DICKENS.name: Andre Dickens
ANDRE DICKENS.background: Mayor of Atlanta, a former Atlanta City Council member who won the Nov. 30, 2021 runoff over Felicia Moore and was re-elected Nov. 4, 2025 with 85 percent.

positions.stance: Ran for re-election on gains in public safety, affordable housing and infrastructure.
Said opposition to the training center had faded and that voters backed him.

ANDRE DICKENS.record: Declined the October 2025 Atlanta Press Club mayoral debate.
endorsements: 2021 runoff: Sharon Gay and Keisha Lance Bottoms (per Wikipedia's list)

MARY NORWOOD.name: Mary Norwood
MARY NORWOOD.background: Two-time Atlanta mayoral candidate (2009, 2017) who described herself as an independent. Finished second in the Nov. 7, 2017 election and lost the Dec. 5, 2017 runoff to Keisha Lance Bottoms with 49.56% after a recount.

FELICIA MOORE.name: Felicia Moore
FELICIA MOORE.background: Former Atlanta City Council president. Finished first in the Nov. 2, 2021 mayoral election with 40.8% and lost the Nov. 30 runoff to Andre Dickens.

sources.t: Wikipedia: 2021 Atlanta mayoral election

BRIAN KEMP.name: Brian Kemp
BRIAN KEMP.background: Governor of Georgia since 2019 and earlier secretary of state. Won the 2018 general election with 50.22% and the 2022 election with 53.4%. As governor he signed the 2021 voting law and bills loosening firearm rules.
